title: Mobile generators and their hookups

blocks.text: During a storm, a utility places mobile generators at critical sites (a hospital feeder, a water plant, a shelter). The fleet has `fleet` generator-hours in all. Site $`s`$ is worth a value per generator-hour and can use at most a number of hours (its demand). A site gets generator-hours **only if** a hookup is built there first, which costs a fixed fee. The planners maximize value less fees.
`build(sites, fleet, big_m, integer)` in `generators.py` already creates the hours $`g_s \ge 0`$, the hookup binaries $`h_s`$, the demand and fleet rows and the objective. Write three things:

items: the hookup row in `build`, one per site, switched by $`h_s`$, using `big_m[s]`;
`tight_m(sites, fleet)`: each site's smallest valid $`M`$, from the rows the model already has (no solve);

`bounds(sites, fleet)`: the LP relaxation's value with $`M = 10^6`$ for every site (`"loose"`), the LP relaxation's value with `tight_m` (`"tight"`), and the MILP optimum with `tight_m` (`"milp"`). Use GLOP for the LPs and HiGHS for the MILP.

blocks.text: The model, with $`v_s`$ the value per hour, $`D_s`$ the demand, $`f_s`$ the fee and $`H`$ the fleet:

\begin{aligned}
\max \;& \textstyle\sum_s v_s\, g_s - \sum_s f_s\, h_s \\
& g_s \ge 0, \quad h_s \in \{0, 1\} && \forall s \\
& g_s \le D_s && \forall s \quad \text{(demand}_s) \\
& \textstyle\sum_s g_s \le H && \text{(fleet)} \\
& \text{?} && \forall s \quad \text{(hookup}_s)
\end{aligned}
Write the hookup row and the formula for $`M_s`$ in this notation first. Before running anything, predict which of the two LP values is higher, and why.

The tests fix a plan by its variables' bounds and ask the solver whether it is allowed, so any correct row passes; two more tests check `tight_m`'s values and the three numbers `bounds` returns. About ten lines.

cases.says: generator-hours at a hooked-up site are allowed, and at a site with no hookup refused
a hooked-up site may use every hour it can, as long as the fleet has them
each site's M is the smaller of its demand and the fleet's hours
the tight M gives a lower LP bound than 1e6, and the MILP optimum is the same

origin.section: A Loose M Weakens the LP Bound; the MILP Optimum Does Not Move

concepts: a loose M raises the LP bound while every valid M gives the same MILP optimum
in the LP relaxation a fee-switched rule costs the fee divided by M per unit over the limit
